gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 390817 Horsedrawn tram on St. Helena Island, 1928.jpg

gallery.source: StateLibQld 2 390817 Horsedrawn tram on St. Helena Island, 1928
gallery.description:
Horsedrawn tram on St. Helena Island, 1928
The horsedrawn tram was used to transport people from the causeway jetty to the prison buildings on the hill. The tram ran on 3'6' guage tracks. Many of the track rails can be seen on the island but have been used as reinforcing for concrete covers on some of the large wells. (Description supplied with photograph.).

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 2 293323 Prisoners making uniforms in the tailors' workshop on St Helena Island, 1911.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 293323 Prisoners making uniforms in the tailors' workshop on St Helena Island, 1911.jpg
gallery.description:
Prisoners making uniforms in the tailors' workshop on St Helena Island, 1911
The tailors' workshop where prison uniforms, police uniforms and any other necessary sewing was done by the convicts. Notice the tailors on the side benches are all sitting cross-legged with the material to be sewn lying across their knees. This was the position used by all tailors in the days of hand tailoring. (Description supplied with photograph.).

gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 293327 Prisoners in the saddlers' shop on St Helena Island, 1911.jpg
gallery.description:
Prisoners in the saddlers' shop on St Helena Island, 1911
The prison leather shop where convicts were kept busy in the manufacture of belts, horse harnesses, saddles, boot and shoe repairs, leather aprons etc. Government regulations did not allow the photographing of prisoners' faces. Notice that only the backs of inmates were shown. (Description supplied with photograph.).

gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 392373 Prisoners working on flax at the old sugar mill site on St. Helena Island, 1912.jpg
gallery.description:
Prisoners working on flax at the old sugar mill site on St. Helena Island, 1912
Sisal hemp raspador and silos used at the penal settlement on St. Helena Island. After the closing down of the sugar mill in 1889, use was then made of the area for turning the raw flax into long soft fibres ready for weaving into rope. (Description supplied with photograph.).

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 2 392393 Signal cannon on St. Helena Island, 1939.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 392393 Signal cannon on St. Helena Island, 1939.jpg
gallery.description:
Signal cannon on St. Helena Island, 1939
This cannon was kept on the island as a tool of warning to any vessels like fishing boats or pleasure craft which seemed to sail too close to the prison. A warning shot would be fired in the general direction of the offending vessel. The cannon is now the property of the Stafford district boy scouts and is standing at their hall. (Description supplied with photograph.).

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 2 392577 Vegetable gardens, H.M. Penal Establishment, St. Helena (Prisioners' garden in foreground), 1911.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 392577 Vegetable gardens, H.M. Penal Establishment, St. Helena (Prisioners' garden in foreground), 1911.jpg
gallery.description:
Vegetable gardens, H.M. Penal Establishment, St. Helena (Prisioners' garden in foreground), 1911
The vegetable garden was quite large, supplying the island's needs. Through most of the life of this island prison, the jail was self-supporting. In fact, during most years a profit was shown on the balance sheet. Water was brought from the wells and then poured over the plants by hand-held watering cans. (Description supplied with photograph).

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 2 392585 Field gang and vegetable gardens at St. Helena Island, 1913.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 392585 Field gang and vegetable gardens at St. Helena Island, 1913.jpg
gallery.description:
Field gang and vegetable gardens at St. Helena Island, 1913
The top insert view shows a prisoners'  field gang at work, while the main photograph shows some of the vegetable gardens at H.M Penal Establishment on St. Helena. The  buildings in the background are: Warders' barracks on right; Chief warder's quarters on left; Mr. Bowden standing in middle of picture. (Description supplied with photograph).

gallery.filename: StateLibQld 2 390813 Ornate fountain on St. Helena Island, 1928.jpg
gallery.title: File:StateLibQld 2 390813 Ornate fountain on St. Helena Island, 1928.jpg
gallery.description:
Ornate fountain on St. Helena Island, 1928.
One of the ornate fountains near the rear of the superintendants's house. When first constructed the fountains blew water high into the sky. To achieve this, selected prisoners were hidden over the edge of a steep bank on the north side of the island. Here a pump was worked vigorously up and down to force water through the fountain jets. The fountain is made of coral. (Description supplied with photograph.).

gallery.description:
Main jail building on Saint Helena, 1928.
